title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Personnel
tiers.description: All Directors, officers, employees and contractors of the Company and its subsidiaries, and any other person notified that the Policy applies to them. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the Closed Period bar, the Front Page Test and the excluded trading list, but not by the clearance, short-term, hedging or secured financing rules.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, members of the MinRes Senior Leadership Team (Executive General Manager role or above, including the Company Secretary), and any other person advised in writing by the Company Secretary (which may be ad hoc, e.g. staff working on a market sensitive matter). Subject to prior written clearance, ad hoc trading prohibitions, the short-term and speculative trading ban, and the hedging and secured financing rules.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: the Chair's Clearance Officer is the Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Directors (other than the Chair of the Board)
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance (Clearance Officer is the Chair of the Board) and for the Listing Rule 3.19A notification and closed-period clearance confirmation obligations.

tiers.name: Other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Designated Persons who are not Directors (and, on the drafting of the hedging section, not key management personnel). Clearance Officer is the Managing Director. This is the tier for which hedging and use of Company securities as loan security is permitted with prior written approval.

tiers.name: key management personnel
tiers.description: Members of the Company's key management personnel, and their Connected Parties, singled out for an absolute ban on arrangements limiting exposure to risk on unvested remuneration or remuneration subject to a holding lock.

tiers.name: Connected Parties
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Designated Person in dealings with the Company or Company securities (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependents), and a company or other entity the Designated Person has an ability to control (which may include family trusts or superannuation funds where the Designated Person is trustee or beneficiary).

definitions.hedging_definition: an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock (key management personnel); transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company (other Designated Persons)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may impose further restrictions on Designated Persons dealing in MinRes securities or securities of other companies by notifying them in writing; additional prohibited periods are imposed when the Company is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A. The Company Secretary may also designate additional persons as Designated Persons in writing on an ad hoc basis. Refusal of clearance or revocation of an approval must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: No express derivatives rule. 'Dealing' extends to creating a derivative over securities and to entering into an agreement to do so, and 'securities' means Division 3 financial products including derivatives, with no venue limit, so an OTC put and call with a bank is a dealing requiring prior written clearance from the Clearance Officer and is barred in Closed Periods. The Closed Period bar separately names 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities'.
rules.evidence: It also extends to subscribing for new securities, exercising options over securities and creating a derivative over securities and includes entering into an agreement to do any of those things

rules.detail: Personnel who are not Designated Persons need no clearance, but must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of MinRes securities during a Closed Period, and may never deal while holding Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Personnel must not deal in the Company's securities, or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, during a Closed Period (unless exceptional circumstances apply).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any arrangement limiting a KMP's exposure to risk on unvested remuneration. Extends to the KMP's Connected Parties.
rules.evidence: A member of the Company's key management personnel, or a Connected Party of such a member, must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The same absolute ban expressly captures remuneration that has vested but 'remains subject to a holding lock', so a collar over holding-locked shares is unavailable to KMP even with approval.
rules.evidence: an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The KMP ban is confined to unvested or holding-locked remuneration and so does not reach freely held vested shares. The approval-gated bullets are addressed to 'Other Designated Persons', leaving it unclear whether they bind KMP; the prudent reading, and the one the Front Page Test supports, is that a KMP hedging vested unrestricted shares needs the same prior written approval from the Clearance Officer.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Persons must not: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company ... unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.

rules.detail: Hedging of any MinRes holding is expressly permitted with prior written approval from the relevant Clearance Officer (Managing Director for non-Director Designated Persons, Chair of the Board for Directors). No security-state distinction is drawn for this tier, and the excluded trading list contemplates a secured lender later selling under such an approved arrangement.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Persons must not: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company; or use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.

rules.detail: The hedging section binds only key management personnel and Designated Persons; Personnel below that level are not addressed, subject only to the insider trading, Closed Period and Front Page Test constraints.

rules.section: Hedging and secured financing arrangements; Definitions (dealing)
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar operates to limit the economic risk of the holding and is also an agreement to dispose of securities, so it is caught twice over and requires prior written approval plus clearance to deal.
rules.evidence: enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company

rules.detail: Any monetisation of unvested or holding-locked KMP remuneration has the effect of limiting exposure to risk and falls within the absolute KMP ban.
rules.evidence: must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Short selling is named as an example of speculative dealing and is banned outright for Designated Persons, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on either: a short-term basis (ie buying and selling within 3 months) ... or a speculative basis (including short selling).

rules.detail: The short-term and speculative trading ban is addressed only to Designated Persons; the Policy is silent on short selling by other Personnel.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the definition of dealing; a stock loan involving a transfer of title would nonetheless be a disposal and so a dealing.

rules.section: Short term or speculative trading; Definitions (dealing)
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD over MinRes securities is a derivative created over securities and so a dealing requiring clearance, but it would in practice be speculative dealing, which is banned for Designated Persons with no approval route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on ... a speculative basis (including short selling).

rules.detail: Margin loans are expressly named and expressly permitted with prior written approval from the relevant Clearance Officer; they are not banned.
rules.evidence: use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer

rules.detail: The KMP paragraph bans only arrangements limiting exposure to unvested or holding-locked remuneration; a margin loan over freely held vested shares is not such an arrangement, so it falls to the approval-gated bullets, which on their face address 'Other Designated Persons'. Prior written approval should be obtained.
rules.evidence: use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer

rules.detail: The secured financing rules bind only Designated Persons and key management personnel; other Personnel are not addressed.

Granting security over MinRes securities is permitted only with prior written approval of the relevant Clearance Officer. Granting security is not itself within the definition of dealing, so the approval requirement, not the clearance regime, is the operative gate; the excluded trading list then protects the lender's later enforcement sale.
rules.evidence: or use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer

rules.detail: No encumbrance rule applies to Personnel who are not Designated Persons, and granting security is not a dealing under the definition.

rules.section: Hedging and secured financing arrangements; Excluded trading (lender disposals)
rules.detail: Using Company securities as security for loans of any kind, expressly including 'for hedging' arrangements, is permitted with prior written approval from the Clearance Officer. The Policy anticipates the funded structure: the excluded trading list carves out a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights where prior written approval was received for entry into the arrangement.
rules.evidence: lender disposals – a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights where prior written approval was received for entry into the arrangement

rules.detail: A pledge alone does not limit exposure to risk, but a funded collar over unvested or holding-locked KMP remuneration does, and is caught by the absolute KMP ban. The Policy does not separately prohibit pledging unvested securities.
rules.evidence: must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: Bright-line buy-and-sell-within-3-months ban, with a single carve-out for the sale of securities allocated on vesting under an employee share scheme outside a Closed Period. No approval route is offered.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on either: a short-term basis (ie buying and selling within 3 months) - except for the sale of Company securities allocated upon vesting under an employee share scheme (provided the dealing is not during a Closed Period)

rules.detail: The short-term trading ban applies only to Designated Persons, though the Policy Overview encourages all Personnel to hold securities on a long-term basis.

exemption_authority: The relevant Clearance Officer (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair of the Board; Chair of the Board for other Directors; Managing Director for other Designated Persons, each able to appoint a delegate) may give prior written approval to deal during a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances, and is the same officer who approves hedging and secured financing arrangements. The Company Secretary may make administrative amendments to the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Other Designated Persons must not ... use Company securities as security for loans, including for hedging and margin loan arrangements unless prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most ASX policies this one does not ban secured financing outright but gates it on a single prior written approval, so the loan leg of a funded collar is available in principle to Directors and other Designated Persons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: lender disposals – a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights where prior written approval was received for entry into the arrangement, is excluded from the operation of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement or physical settlement sale is excluded from the Policy, including during a Closed Period, provided the collar and loan were approved up front, which removes the usual fatal forced-sale risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A member of the Company's key management personnel, or a Connected Party of such a member, must not enter into an arrangement which would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration that has not vested or remains subject to a holding lock.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For KMP the collar can only be written over shares that have both vested and come off any holding lock, and no approval can cure a collar over unvested or locked remuneration.

bespoke_clauses.topic: drafting gap for KMP on vested shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval-gated bullets on limiting economic risk and using securities as loan security are addressed to 'Other Designated Persons', while the preceding paragraph addresses key management personnel only in respect of unvested or holding-locked remuneration.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no express rule permitting or prohibiting a KMP hedging or pledging fully vested unrestricted shares, so a bank should require the Clearance Officer's written approval and, ideally, a Board confirmation of the reading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not deal in Company securities on ... a speculative basis (including short selling).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A written call and purchased put must be documented as risk management over a long-held position rather than a speculative or short position, and the collar should be delta-neutral rather than net short.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a short-term basis (ie buying and selling within 3 months)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar tenor and any unwind or roll should sit outside a three-month buy-and-sell pattern in the underlying shares, and shares recently acquired should not be collared and delivered within three months.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Periods run from the end of the financial year, half year, September quarter and March quarter until the first trading day after release of the corresponding results or quarterly report.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: MinRes has four blackouts a year because of quarterly reporting, so the windows for pricing and executing the collar and any roll are materially narrower than at a half-yearly reporter.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Clearance Officer ... may revoke their approval at any time. An approved dealing must occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing, documentation and execution of the collar must complete inside five business days of clearance, and the bank bears the risk that clearance is revoked before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Clearance Officer ... may in their discretion grant or refuse the request, or impose conditions on the dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval for the collar may come with conditions such as tenor, strike levels, disclosure or a maximum proportion of the holding, which must be capable of being reflected in the confirmation and loan documents.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings that would not satisfy the Front Page Test should not occur, even where the dealing may not strictly be prohibited under this Policy or otherwise at law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An anti-avoidance overlay that can defeat a technically compliant collar on reputational grounds, so the structure should be capable of clean public description and, for Directors, of Appendix 3Y disclosure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Personnel must not deal in the Company's securities, or in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities, during a Closed Period (unless exceptional circumstances apply).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, unwind, roll and cash settlement of the OTC options are themselves barred in Closed Periods for everyone, not just Designated Persons, absent an exceptional-circumstances approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Parties only deal in securities in circumstances where the Designated Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a family trust, controlled company or superannuation fund does not avoid the approval and clearance requirements.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must immediately notify the Company Secretary of any dealings in the Company's securities when any such dealings occur.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into the collar must be reported to the Company Secretary immediately and, for Directors, will feed a Listing Rule 3.19A Appendix 3Y disclosure of the change in the nature of their interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: pre-determined investment or divestment plans – dealings under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided by the Board and ... the plan cannot be cancelled during a Closed Period except in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Offers an alternative route: physical settlement of the collar could be structured as a Board-cleared non-discretionary plan so settlement is not blocked by a Closed Period.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at MinRes, which is unusual. The Policy does not ban secured financing or hedging outright: 'Other Designated Persons' may both limit the economic risk of their MinRes holding and use MinRes securities as security for loans, expressly including hedging and margin loan arrangements, provided prior written approval is obtained from the relevant Clearance Officer (Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair, Chair of the Board for other Directors, Managing Director for everyone else), and the excluded trading list then protects the bank's enforcement sale by carving out a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights where that prior approval was obtained. The hard limits are that key management personnel and their Connected Parties can never hedge remuneration that is unvested or subject to a holding lock, so the collar must be written only over shares that have vested and come off any lock, and the derivative legs are themselves dealings requiring clearance, executed within five business days, outside the four annual Closed Periods (financial year, half year, September and March quarters) and any Listing Rule 3.1A blackout. The structure must not look speculative or short, should avoid a three-month buy-and-sell pattern, must survive the Front Page Test, and must be notified to the Company Secretary immediately (with Appendix 3Y disclosure for Directors). A drafting gap leaves it unclear whether the approval-gated bullets bind KMP in respect of fully vested unrestricted shares, so a bank should insist on written Clearance Officer approval covering both the derivative legs and the security in every case.
